title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the Union Civil Protection Mechanism and Union support for health emergency preparedness and response, and repealing Decision No 1313/2013/EU (Union Civil Protection Mechanism)
section: Article 26 – paragraph 1 | Article 26 – paragraph 1 a (new) | Article 26 – paragraph 1 b (new) | Article 26 – paragraph 1 c (new) | Article 26 – paragraph 2 | Article 26 – paragraph 2 a (new) | Article 26 – paragraph 2 b (new) | Article 26 – paragraph 4 a (new) | Article 26 – paragraph 4 b (new)
part_text: 1. Without prejudice to Article 25, a Crisis support Hub (‘the Hub’) is hereby established within the ERCC. It shall monitor crises and potential crises on permanent basis, enhance preparedness, and upon activation of response in accordance with Article 29, facilitates Union-level operational coordination, and provides Union support to crises response. The Hub shall operate within the ERCC and use its capabilities, including its analytical and scientific capabilities, situational awareness, and 24/7 operational capacity for cross-sectoral crises, complementing and without prejudice to the civil protection functions of the ERCC under Article 25. The ERCC shall provide the operational continuity, coordination infrastructure and communication systems necessary for the activities of the Hub. / 1a. The Hub shall, on a permanent basis: (a) maintain and periodically update the organisational framework referred to in paragraph 1c, (b) establish and regularly review its readiness and activation protocols, (c) monitor relevant risk indicators related to potential crises, for the purpose of maintaining readiness, (d) evaluate responses crises in accordance with Article 29 to enhance future preparedness and draw lessons learned, (e) establish a framework and receive notifications about crises sent through relevant Union instruments. / 1b. The Hub shall maintain a pre-established organisational framework, to be mobilised upon activation of response in accordance with Article 29, comprising: (a) the capabilities of the ERCC referred to in paragraph 1b; (b) a roster of relevant Union structures, agencies and subject-matter experts; (c) the national contact points designated by Member States pursuant to paragraph 1c; (d) relevant external experts identified in advance. / 1c. Member States shall designate national contact points for the purposes of this Article and inform the Commission accordingly. The Commission shall maintain and regularly update a register of those contact points. Member States may designate the same contact points for the purposes of this paragraph and Article 25(5). The Hub shall coordinate with its designated national contact points as appropriate. / 2. The Hub shall closely cooperate with the EEAS Crisis Response Centre in the external dimension of crises, with respect to their roles and competences, and in full respect of the Humanitarian Aid Regulation and applicable rules of international humanitarian law. / 2a. The Hub shall, where relevant, cooperate with the Union structures and agencies responsible for preparedness and response to serious cross-border threats to health, in full respect of their respective mandates and of the governance framework established under Regulation (EU) 2022/2371. / 2b. The Hub shall, where relevant, use the support and the expertise provided by the Knowledge Network referred to in Article 18. / 4a. Following the activation of response of the Hub, the Commission shall report back to the European Parliament and the Council. / 4b. The Commission shall also report annually to the European Parliament and the Council on the activities of the Hub, including the number and nature of crises for which the Hub was activated, the coordination measures undertaken, and the lessons learned for preparedness and response.
